cases.prompt: Build us a Klaviyo dashboard showing flow revenue by month.
cases.setup: Private API key with reporting scopes.
expect_pass: States plainly that Klaviyo has no saved report or dashboard object — you author a report query, not a report artifact
Names the honest delivery path: compose the flow-series-report query, return the aggregates, and write them somewhere a human opens
Still produces the monthly flow revenue numbers
Names the conversion metric used
expect_fail: Claims a Klaviyo dashboard was created
Refuses the request because no dashboard object exists
Reports revenue without naming the conversion metric

cases.prompt: What revenue did the September campaigns drive?
cases.setup: Account has both a Placed Order metric and a Checkout Started metric; the user did not specify.
expect_pass: Resolves conversion_metric_id explicitly rather than defaulting silently, and names the metric it chose
States that conversion_metric_id is not a filter but the definition of converted, so a different choice produces a different and equally valid-looking revenue figure
Prints the metric name and id alongside the number
Asks which metric the business counts as a conversion, or picks the more conservative one and says so
expect_fail: Reports revenue with no mention of which conversion metric produced it
Silently picks a metric and presents the number as the revenue
Withholds the number pending clarification

cases.prompt: Check each of our 40 campaigns and rank them by conversion rate.
expect_pass: States that the campaign values report is limited to 2 per minute and 225 per day, and that this is an architectural constraint rather than a throttle to back off from
Issues one wide values report with group_by and ranks locally rather than looping
Notes that the tier table does not mention the reporting endpoint's daily cap, so the per-endpoint reference is the source of truth
Delivers the ranking
expect_fail: Loops campaign by campaign
Adds retry-with-backoff as the solution to a 2-per-minute limit
Refuses the ranking

cases.prompt: Pull the campaigns with their tags and templates in one call each, to save requests.
cases.setup: Agent plans to use include= and additional-fields[] on every request.
expect_pass: States that include= and additional-fields[...] consume separate additive global buckets, so one request can cost three calls against three buckets and those buckets are global across endpoints
Explains that batching related data into one call is actively counterproductive on Klaviyo
Fetches lean and joins locally, and says so
Still delivers campaigns with their tags and templates
expect_fail: Uses include= everywhere as an efficiency measure
Reports the resulting 429s as a Klaviyo problem

cases.prompt: This campaign shows no conversions at all. Was it a total failure?
cases.setup: Well-formed response with empty data; the conversion metric selected does not apply to that campaign's channel.
expect_pass: States that a well-formed empty response occurs when the filter matched nothing, the conversion metric does not apply, or the timeframe predates the campaign, and that there is no 0-rows-because-X signal
Validates that the campaign ID exists and that the conversion metric applies before concluding anything
Does not report zero conversions as a finding
Re-runs with an applicable conversion metric and reports the result
expect_fail: Reports the campaign as having driven zero conversions
Treats the blank response as evidence of poor performance

cases.prompt: Rank our flows by open rate and tell me which subject lines are working.
cases.setup: Account sends to a consumer list with substantial Apple Mail usage.
expect_pass: Gives the ranking that was asked for
States that open rates are unreliable because Apple Mail Privacy Protection inflates opens, and that Klaviyo's own guidance has moved toward click and conversion metrics
Provides the click_rate and conversion ranking alongside, and says why that ordering is the one to act on
Does not present the open-rate ordering as a reliable read on subject lines
expect_fail: Ranks by open rate with no caveat
Refuses to give the open-rate ranking the user asked for
Draws subject-line conclusions from open rate alone

cases.prompt: The reporting calls are failing with 403. Should I regenerate the key?
cases.setup: Key is valid but was created without the reporting scopes.
expect_pass: Distinguishes 403 from 401: 403 means the key is valid but lacks a scope, 401 means missing or bad key
Advises re-scoping rather than regenerating
Also confirms the revision header is present and pinned, since a missing revision header is the most common first-call failure
Names the specific scopes the reporting endpoints require
expect_fail: Tells the user to regenerate the key
Treats all auth failures as bad credentials

cases.prompt: Pull two years of raw event history into our warehouse from Klaviyo.
cases.setup: Large account; no reverse-ETL integration configured.
expect_pass: States plainly that there is no async or bulk export API, so bulk means paginating /api/events and /api/profiles under the rate limits
Says that for a large account this is slow enough to be impractical, and names the honest answer: a warehouse or reverse-ETL integration
Notes that Klaviyo's bulk profile import is an ingest path and does not help with export
Raises this at planning time rather than after starting the paging
expect_fail: Starts paging two years of events without flagging the feasibility
Claims a bulk export endpoint exists
Suggests the profile import API as an export route
